newsitem.title: USA: Virginia Power says 9,400 still lack power.
newsitem.headline: Virginia Power says 9,400 still lack power.

text.p: Virginia Power Co, a subsidiary of Dominion Resources Inc, said Tuesday 9,400 customers are still without power in its service district in the aftermath of Hurricane Fran.
The storm, after racing across neighboring North Carolina, headed right into Virginia Power's service territory early Friday, where it knocked 415,000 customers off the grid.
"That is twice as many customers as we've ever had out during a storm," said company spokesman Charles Taylor.
He said the utility's preliminary estimates put the cost of restoring power after Fran at $10 million to $15 million.
Central Virginia, especially Richmond, bore the brunt of the storm, where strong winds, heavy rains, and soggy soil resulted in a huge number of trees toppling power lines.
About 7,200 customers in and around Richmond are still without power. "But we expect most of them to be back by midnight tonight," Taylor said.
A 115 kilovolt transmission line in the Shenandoah Valley, one of seven Virginia Power high-voltage lines knocked out by the storm, is still out of service.
Damage to the company's generating facilities was limited mostly to debris tossed about by the storm. A substation in Newport News was knocked off line when a nearby rooftop was blown onto the site.
One of the two 741 megawatt (MW) reactors at the Surry nuclear power station was also shut as a result of the storm when debris clogged its coolant water intake channel.
The unit, at Gravel Neck, Va., on the James River, has since been restarted and is producing at full power.
The company said it anticipated no problems meeting power demand on its system Tuesday, estimating a seasonally normal peak load of about 12,600 MW this evening.
"As far as I know we are not buying any power in the spot market to meet demand," Taylor said.
-- J Jelter, New York Power Desk + 1 212 859 1621
